plain_english_title: Survivor DIC Monthly Benefits: Service-Connected Cause of Death (§ 1310), the 10-Year Total-Disability Rule (§ 1318) & PACT Act Re-Evaluations
what_this_means: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) is a tax-free monthly benefit paid to eligible surviving spouses, dependent children, and low-income parents. Importantly, there are TWO completely separate paths to qualify—and VA denials often check only part of the picture: (1) Direct or Contributory Death (38 U.S.C. § 1310; 38 C.F.R. § 3.312), where a service-connected condition (including PACT Act or Agent Orange presumptions) was either the primary cause of death OR contributed substantially and materially to death—even if left off the death certificate; and (2) Total-Disability DIC (38 U.S.C. § 1318; 38 C.F.R. § 3.22), paid regardless of the cause of death when the Veteran held (or was legally entitled to receive) a 100% or TDIU rating for at least 10 continuous years before death (5 years from military discharge, or 1 year for Former POWs). In addition, under PACT Act § 204 (38 U.S.C. § 1305; 38 C.F.R. § 3.33), survivors whose earlier DIC claims were denied before a post-August 10, 2022 presumption (such as hypertension or burn-pit cancers) can re-elect DIC with retroactive effective dates back to the original denied DIC claim.
record_clues: A DIC denial letter (VA Form 21P-534EZ) relying solely on the one-page death certificate without reviewing final hospital/ICU records showing how service-connected heart, lung, kidney, diabetes, or mental health conditions hastened death (§ 3.312(c)).

A Veteran who died of a non-service-connected cause at 70%–90% (or with fewer than 10 years at 100%/TDIU), where correcting a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) in a lifetime decision (§ 3.22(b)(1)) or adding missing military records (§ 3.22(b)(2) / § 3.156(c)) pushes 100% or TDIU past the 10-year mark.

A previously denied DIC claim where the Veteran died of complications from hypertension, MGUS, expanded Agent Orange service (Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Guam, Blue Water Navy), or Gulf War / post-9/11 burn-pit illnesses (38 C.F.R. § 3.33).

A granted DIC award missing the extra monthly 8-year 'kicker' (§ 1311(a)(2)), surviving spouse Aid & Attendance / Housebound add-ons (§ 1311(c)–(d)), the 2-year transitional benefit for minor children (§ 1311(f)), or full military Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) restoration after Congress repealed the SBP-DIC offset effective January 1, 2023.
important_cautions: How Post-2000 'Hypothetical' § 1318 DIC Works (38 C.F.R. § 3.22(b)): Since VA amended § 3.22 on January 21, 2000 (65 FR 3388, upheld in Rodriguez and Tarver), if the Veteran did not already hold a 10-year 100%/TDIU rating at death, a survivor cannot argue open-ended 'hypothetical' entitlement from scratch—entitlement under § 3.22(b) requires showing a prior lifetime VA claim plus either CUE in a final lifetime decision (§ 3.22(b)(1)), newly associated official service department records (§ 3.22(b)(2)), or a specified military retired-pay/withholding nonpayment rule.

Judicial Reinterpretation CUE Limit (George v. McDonough): When using § 3.22(b)(1) CUE to challenge a deceased Veteran's final lifetime decision, later judicial reinterpretations cannot establish CUE under 38 C.F.R. § 20.1403(e), and pre-July 21, 1992 lifetime decisions are evaluated on the physical C-file record at that time (Damrel v. Brown).

8-Year DIC Kicker Marriage Requirement: To receive the extra monthly § 1311(a)(2) 8-year allowance, the Veteran must have been rated totally disabled (100% or TDIU) for 8 continuous years immediately preceding death AND married to the surviving spouse for those exact same 8 continuous years.

Wrongful-Death Settlement Offset Difference (§ 1318 vs. § 1310): If a survivor received a civil wrongful-death or Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) recovery, 38 U.S.C. § 1318(d) requires offsetting non-service-connected § 1318 DIC, whereas proving direct/contributory service-connected death under § 1310 avoids the § 1318(d) non-FTCA private-tort offset (VAOPGCPREC 3-97).
questions_for_representative: Did VA obtain the final hospitalization, ICU, or autopsy records to evaluate whether a service-connected condition (especially one affecting a vital organ at 100% under § 3.312(c)(3)) contributed substantially and materially to death?

If my spouse's DIC claim was previously denied before August 10, 2022, does a PACT Act presumption (such as hypertension or burn-pit cancer) qualify me for retroactive re-evaluation back to my original DIC claim date under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33?

If my spouse had fewer than 10 years at 100%/TDIU on paper at death, was there a void rating reduction, newly associated service record (§ 3.22(b)(2)), or lifetime CUE (§ 3.22(b)(1)) that would establish 10 continuous years of total disability?

Did my DIC award letter properly include all applicable § 1311 add-ons (8-year kicker, spouse Aid & Attendance/Housebound, minor-child transitional benefit), and was my claim filed within 1 year of death for a date-of-death effective date (§ 5110(d))?
